properties.name: camel.component.avro.autowired-enabled
properties.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

properties.name: camel.component.avro.bridge-error-handler
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: camel.component.avro.configuration
properties.description: A shared configuration that every endpoint copies as its starting point. The options of the endpoint URI override its values. The option is a org.apache.camel.component.avro.AvroConfiguration type.

properties.name: camel.component.avro.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable auto configuration of the avro component. This is enabled by default.

properties.name: camel.component.avro.lazy-start-producer
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: camel.component.avro.protocol
properties.description: The Avro protocol (org.apache.avro.Protocol) that defines the messages, such as the PROTOCOL field of a class generated by the Avro compiler. Set this option or protocolClassName: the endpoint fails to start without a protocol. Camel adds the packages of the protocol to the trusted packages of Avro, which apply to the whole JVM: see serializablePackages. The option is a org.apache.avro.Protocol type.

properties.name: camel.component.avro.protocol-class-name
properties.description: The fully qualified name of the class that defines the protocol. For a class generated by the Avro compiler, its static PROTOCOL field is used; for any other class or interface, Avro reflection builds the protocol and reflectionProtocol is turned on. Ignored when protocol is set. Camel adds the package of the class to the trusted packages of Avro, which apply to the whole JVM: see serializablePackages.

properties.name: camel.component.avro.protocol-location
properties.description: The location of an Avro protocol file in JSON (.avpr), such as classpath:my-protocol.avpr or file:/path/my-protocol.avpr. Used when neither protocol nor protocolClassName is set. Records of the protocol use the classes generated by the Avro compiler when they are on the classpath. Camel adds the packages of the protocol to the trusted packages of Avro, which apply to the whole JVM: see serializablePackages.

properties.name: camel.component.avro.reflection-protocol
properties.description: Whether the protocol is a reflect protocol, built by Avro reflection from a Java interface, rather than one from classes generated by the Avro compiler. When true, the consumer and producer use the Avro reflect responder and requestor. Set it together with protocol: with protocolClassName it is turned on for a class without a PROTOCOL field.

properties.name: camel.component.avro.serializable-packages
properties.description: Comma-separated list of additional packages that contain trusted Avro model classes. Avro 1.12+ validates classes resolved from schemas; Camel automatically trusts org.apache.avro for IPC and packages derived from the configured protocol. Use this option for any additional model packages not inferred from the protocol. Avro has one class validator for the whole JVM. A package trusted by one endpoint is trusted for all Avro class resolution in the JVM, by every endpoint, Avro data format and Camel context, and stays trusted until the JVM is restarted: stopping the endpoint or the route does not remove it.

properties.name: camel.component.avro.single-parameter
properties.description: Whether the consumer sets the message body to the one parameter of the called message, instead of an Object array of all parameters. The endpoint fails to start if the message, or any message of the protocol when messageName is not set, does not have exactly one parameter.

properties.name: camel.component.avro.uri-authority
properties.description: Deprecated: not used. The component sets it to the host and port of the endpoint URI, and a value set on the endpoint or the component has no effect. Deprecation note: Not used; the host and port of the endpoint URI are used instead
